architecture.mechanism: Torsional vibration damper integrated within a hydrodynamic torque converter, using a turbine hub coaxially arranged with the rotating shaft and non-rotatably fixed to the turbine wheel, so torsional oscillations transmitted between the turbine and the output shaft are absorbed by the damper stage rather than passed into the driveline.
architecture.intervention: Retrofit or service-fit a torsional vibration damper assembly into the torque converter of the 2020 Toyota Camry's automatic transmission, anchoring the damper stage to a turbine hub fixed non-rotatably to the turbine wheel, with damper springs/hysteresis elements tuned to the engine's torsional excitation order and the lock-up clutch shudder frequency band.
architecture.expected_effect: Torsional excitation from the engine and lock-up clutch slip is damped before reaching the transmission input shaft, reducing the resonant torsional vibration that manifests as torque converter shudder and vehicle vibration, with improved durability under high-mileage service.
architecture.falsification_test: On a transmission dynamometer or vehicle road test with torsional accelerometers on the input shaft, compare vibration amplitude at the shudder frequency (typically ~20-60 Hz under lock-up clutch slip) before and after damper installation; the mechanism is falsified if torsional amplitude and vehicle vibration are not reduced by a statistically significant margin, or if the damper stage fails fatigue life targets (e.g., < full high-mileage service interval) under cyclic torsional loading.
